```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/_tools.R")

# readr rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA
menu <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
subgroups <- readr::read_csv("data/display_subgroups.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
names_tab <- readr::read_csv("data/display_names.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
marks <- readr::read_csv("data/reference_marks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
housing <- readr::read_csv("data/housing_emails.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
original <- readr::read_csv("data/housing_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Fixed decimals and a true minus sign; signed shifts carry a plus sign
fmt <- \(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) |> sub(pattern = "^-", replacement = "−")
sgn <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(dplyr::if_else(x > 0, "+", ""), fmt(x, d))
pct <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(fmt(x, d), "%")
pe <- \(p) dplyr::case_when(p < 0.0001 ~ "p < 0.0001", p < 0.001 ~ paste("p =", fmt(p, 4)),
                            .default = paste("p =", fmt(p, 3)))

ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
dv <- \(axis, option, col) deviations[[col]][deviations$axis == axis & deviations$option == option]
out <- \(o, cn, col) outcomes[[col]][outcomes$outcome == o & outcomes$contrast == cn]
sub_ <- \(start, col) subgroups[[col]][startsWith(subgroups$subgroup, start)]
grp <- \(g, col) names_tab[[col]][names_tab$level == "group" & names_tab$group == g]
mark <- \(id, col) marks[[col]][marks$id == id]

n_dec <- dplyr::n_distinct(menu$axis)
varying <- names(SPEC_AXES)
fixed_axes <- setdiff(unique(menu$axis), varying)

# Bounced emails counted as unanswered: every email sent, against its twin on
# the curve, which counts only the delivered emails
bounced_twin <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                             uncoded = "not_named", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))
bounced_sent <- housing |>
  datawizard::data_filter(group %in% c("white", "hispanic")) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hisp = as.integer(group == "hispanic"), y = as.integer(reply %in% 1 & named %in% 1))
bounced_fit <- stats::lm(y ~ hisp, data = bounced_sent)
bounced_b <- 100 * unname(stats::coef(bounced_fit)["hisp"])
bounced_n <- housing |>
  datawizard::data_filter(is.na(reply)) |>
  datawizard::data_summary(n = n(), by = "group")
bounced_by <- \(g) bounced_n$n[bounced_n$group == g]
no_thirds <- housing |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!stats::complete.cases(pop_third, poverty_third, black_third, hispanic_third)) |>
  nrow()
# The twin of the reference specification that counts every delivered email
all_twin <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                         uncoded = "drop", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))

# The sex of the name added to the reference specification, with HC2 errors
# from parameters and sandwich
sex_frame <- spec_frame(housing, "white", "replies", "drop")
sex_fit <- stats::lm(y ~ hisp + name_sex, data = sex_frame)
sex_b <- 100 * unname(stats::coef(sex_fit)["hisp"])
sex_p <- parameters::model_parameters(sex_fit, vcov = "HC2") |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Parameter == "hisp") |>
  datawizard::data_extract("p")

# The chi-square test of 8PTRZ on the public file of the OAs, with and without
# the continuity correction that chisq.test() applies to a 2 x 2 table
chi_tab <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Response_Dichotomous == 1 & !is.na(ProperName)) |>
  stats::xtabs(formula = ~ startsWith(TreatmentGroup, "Hispanic") + ProperName, data = _)
chi_yates <- stats::chisq.test(chi_tab)
chi_plain <- stats::chisq.test(chi_tab, correct = FALSE)

logit_or <- curve |>
  datawizard::data_filter(model == "logit") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(or = exp(coef))
three_twin <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "replies",
                                                           uncoded = "drop", model = "logit", adjust = "place_ethnic"))
```

This page sets out every decision that an analysis of the claim has to make, the options that each decision offers, and whether each option answers the claim. The claim, in the wording that SCORE took from the paper of the original authors (OAs) [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect], is that "Hispanic housing applicants were ... less likely to be greeted by name than were ... white counterparts". The [background page](background.qmd) sets out the experiment, the five reanalyses and the data.

`r stringr::str_to_sentence(xfun::numbers_to_words(n_dec))` decisions stand between the data and a verdict. For each option the course has asked whether it is a defensible way of answering this claim, and the options that are defensible have been combined into the `r nrow(curve)` specifications of the curve of the claim. The options that are not stay on this page, because each of them answers a different question, answers this one less well, checks an answer that the curve already holds, or cannot be fitted on the public file, and working out which applies is a large part of understanding what the claim asks. `data/menu_options.csv` holds the options with the reason for each ([codebook](data/menu_options_codebook.md)), and the helpers of the browser lab and the workspace read it to explain why an option off the curve is refused.

## The decision map {#map}

```{r}
#| include: false
# Data for the decision map, read once at render: every option of the menu,
# the curve of the claim, every option of the curve against its twins, and the
# displays that hold the options off the curve at the reference settings. All
# of it is aggregate, and the twins are paired in the browser from the curve.
# readr rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA
menu <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange(c("b_pp", "spec_id")) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(rank = 1:n())
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
subgroups <- readr::read_csv("data/display_subgroups.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(curve) == 64, sum(curve$is_reference) == 1)

fallback_titles <- c(
  "background.qmd" = "Housing and racial bias",
  "menu.qmd" = "Specification menu",
  "curve.qmd" = "Specification curve",
  "companion/experiments.qmd" = "Audit experiments",
  "companion/binary-outcomes.qmd" = "Binary outcomes"
)
# page titles without their Markdown emphasis; a page not yet written takes
# the title of its navbar entry
page_title <- \(f) {
  title <- if (file.exists(f)) rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(f)$title
  title <- title %||% unname(fallback_titles[f])  # %||% of base R, 4.4 and later
  if (is.na(title)) f else gsub("*", "", title, fixed = TRUE)
}

# taught_on is a path from the project root, where this page sits, so it links as it stands
menu_js <- menu |>
  datawizard::data_select(c("axis", "level", "option", "label", "on_curve", page = "taught_on", "reason",
                            "decision", "stage", "judgement", "phrase", "estimates", "explanation"))
pages <- unique(menu_js$page) |>
  purrr::set_names() |>
  purrr::map(page_title)

curve_js <- curve |>
  datawizard::data_modify(
    b_pp = round(b_pp, 3), se_pp = round(se_pp, 3), coef = round(coef, 4),
    stat = round(stat, 3), p = signif(p, 3), p_ri = signif(p_ri, 3),
    r = round(r, 4), rate_hisp = round(rate_hisp, 2), rate_comp = round(rate_comp, 2)
  ) |>
  datawizard::data_select(c("spec_id", "comparison", "population", "uncoded", "model", "adjust",
                            "b_pp", "se_pp", "coef", "stat_type", "stat", "df", "p", "p_ri", "r", "n",
                            "rate_hisp", "rate_comp", "rank", ref = "is_reference"))

# the options off the curve that a display beside the curve holds, each fitted
# as a difference in proportions with HC2 errors at the reference settings
display <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  outcomes |>
    datawizard::data_filter(contrast == "hispanic" & outcome %in% c("reply", "reply24")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(axis = "outcome", option = outcome, b_pp, p, n,
                     note = dplyr::if_else(outcome == "reply",
                                           "Hispanic against white names, the share of delivered emails that drew any reply",
                                           "Hispanic against white names, the share of replies that came within 24 hours")),
  outcomes |>
    datawizard::data_filter(outcome == "named" & contrast == "black") |>
    dplyr::transmute(axis = "comparison", option = "black", b_pp, p, n,
                     note = "Black against white names, the share of coded replies that opened with the name"),
  subgroups |>
    datawizard::data_filter(startsWith(subgroup, "male") | startsWith(subgroup, "female") |
                              startsWith(subgroup, "replies from officials")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(axis = dplyr::if_else(startsWith(subgroup, "replies"), "officials", "names"),
                     option = dplyr::case_when(startsWith(subgroup, "male") ~ "male",
                                               startsWith(subgroup, "female") ~ "female",
                                               .default = "hispanic"),
                     b_pp, p, n,
                     note = dplyr::case_when(
                       option == "male" ~ "Santiago against Brett, the share of coded replies that opened with the name",
                       option == "female" ~ "Gabriela against Emily, the share of coded replies that opened with the name",
                       .default = "Hispanic against white names, among the coded replies from officials with Hispanic names"
                     ))
) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(b_pp = round(b_pp, 2), p = signif(p, 3))

ojs_define(menu_raw = menu_js, curve_raw = curve_js, dev_raw = deviations,
           display_raw = display, pages_raw = pages)
```

The map lays out the decisions in the order in which an analyst meets them on the way from the data to a verdict: which emails enter the comparison, what is compared, against which names, with which model, and how the answer is tested and reported. Each decision shows all its options, those on the curve of 64 specifications and those off it. The map opens on the reference specification, the raw gap of the paper between Hispanic and white names among the replies.

Selecting an option rewrites the estimand statement, with the phrases that the choice changed marked, and opens a description of the option: what it estimates, whether it answers the claim, what it does to the estimate against its twins on the curve, and where in the course it is taught. For a selection on the curve, the verdict gives its estimate, the two shares, its test and its rank among the 64; for a selection off the curve, the reason. Nothing is fitted in the browser, and every number is read from the files under `data/` that the course pipeline writes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Data and constants of the map. This chunk displays nothing: a named cell
// whose value is not a DOM node would otherwise print as an inspector line.
menu = transpose(menu_raw)
curve = transpose(curve_raw)
devRows = transpose(dev_raw)
displays = transpose(display_raw)
VARY = ["comparison", "population", "uncoded", "model", "adjust"]
CHECK_AXES = ["inference", "scale"]
curveKey = d => VARY.map(a => d[a]).join("|")
curveIndex = new Map(curve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))

DM = {
  return {
    stages: [
      {id: "data", title: "The emails", note: "Which emails enter the comparison, with which names and from which officials, and what happens to the emails that bounced."},
      {id: "outcome", title: "The outcome", note: "What is compared between the groups of emails, and how the replies without a greeting code count."},
      {id: "comparison", title: "The comparison", note: "Which names the Hispanic names are set against."},
      {id: "model", title: "Model and adjustment", note: "How the difference is estimated, and which covariates the model holds."},
      {id: "inference", title: "The test and the scale", note: "How uncertain the estimate is said to be, and on which scale it is reported."}
    ],
    colour: {outcome: "#0e3b6a", comparison: "#2a5d8f", names: "#4a78ab", population: "#0f6b6b", officials: "#2b8585",
             uncoded: "#4a7a3f", bounced: "#4a7a3f", model: "#8c5a10", adjust: "#7b6a8f", inference: "#7b6a8f", scale: "#7b6a8f"},
    levelName: {estimand: "The question", measurement: "Measurement", estimation: "The model"},
    levelShort: {estimand: "Question", measurement: "Measurement", estimation: "Model"},
    judgement: {kept: "On the curve", other_question: "Another question", weaker_answer: "A weaker answer", check: "A check", unavailable: "Not in the public file"},
    domainB: [-32, 2]
  };
}

// numbers as the site prints them: fixed decimals and a true minus sign
fmtB = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(1)
fmtShift = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : x > 0 ? "+" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(2)
fmtR = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)
fmtStat = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(2)
fmtP = p => p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : p < 0.001 ? p.toFixed(4) : p.toFixed(3)
// "p = 0.021" or "p < 0.0001", so that a bound never follows an equals sign
pEq = p => p < 0.0001 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${fmtP(p)}`
fmtPct = x => x.toFixed(1) + "%"
```


::: {.column-screen-inset}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
decisionMap = {
  const opt = (axis, code) => menu.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
  const optionsOf = axis => menu.filter(d => d.axis === axis);
  const axesOfStage = id => [...new Set(menu.filter(d => d.stage === id).map(d => d.axis))];
  const ALL_AXES = DM.stages.flatMap(st => axesOfStage(st.id));
  const col = axis => DM.colour[axis];
  const el = (tag, attrs, ...kids) => {
    const n = document.createElement(tag);
    if (attrs) for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) {
      if (k === "class") n.className = v;
      else if (k === "text") n.textContent = v;
      else if (k === "style") n.setAttribute("style", v);
      else n.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
    for (const kid of kids) if (kid !== null && kid !== undefined) n.append(kid);
    return n;
  };
  const pageLink = file => el("a", {href: file.replace(/\.qmd$/, ".html")}, pages_raw[file] || file);
  const baselineOf = axis => (devRows.find(d => d.axis === axis) || {}).baseline;

  // ---- state: one option per decision, starting from the reference specification
  const refRow = curve.find(d => d.ref === true);
  const REF = {};
  for (const a of ALL_AXES) REF[a] = (optionsOf(a).find(o => o.on_curve === true) || optionsOf(a)[0]).option;
  for (const a of VARY) REF[a] = refRow[a];
  let sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let latest = null;
  let prevText = null;

  const isOn = (s, a) => opt(a, s[a]).on_curve === true;
  const offAxes = s => ALL_AXES.filter(a => !isOn(s, a));
  const curveRowOf = s => { const k = curveIndex.get(curveKey(s)); return k === undefined ? null : curve[k]; };
  const recipe = d => VARY.map(a => opt(a, d[a]).label).join("; ");

  // ---- the estimand statement, as segments that can be compared with the last one
  function statement(s) {
    const o = a => opt(a, s[a]);
    const cap = t => t.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + t.slice(1);
    const seg = (key, text, lv) => ({key, text, lv});
    const pair = s.comparison === "black" ? "Black names and white names" : `Hispanic names and ${o("comparison").phrase}`;
    return {
      question: [
        seg("population", cap(o("population").phrase), "l1"), ", ", seg("names", o("names").phrase, "l1"), ", ",
        seg("officials", o("officials").phrase, "l1"), ", the difference in the share that drew ", seg("outcome", o("outcome").phrase, "l1"),
        " between ", seg("comparison", pair, "l1"), " (", seg("uncoded", o("uncoded").phrase, "l2"), ", ",
        seg("bounced", o("bounced").phrase, "l2"), ")."
      ],
      method: [
        "Estimated with ", seg("model", o("model").phrase, "l3"), ", ", seg("adjust", o("adjust").phrase, "l3"),
        ", tested by ", seg("inference", o("inference").phrase, "l3"), " and reported ", seg("scale", o("scale").phrase, "l3"), "."
      ]
    };
  }
  function renderSegments(target, parts) {
    target.replaceChildren();
    for (const p of parts) {
      if (typeof p === "string") { target.append(p); continue; }
      const span = el("span", {class: `dm-seg ${p.lv}`, style: `--c:${col(p.key)}`, text: p.text});
      const changed = prevText !== null && prevText[p.key] !== undefined && prevText[p.key] !== p.text;
      target.append(changed ? el("mark", {class: "dm-changed"}, span) : span);
    }
  }

  // ---- what the selection gives
  function verdictOf(s) {
    const off = offAxes(s);
    const blocking = off.filter(a => !(CHECK_AXES.includes(a) && opt(a, s[a]).judgement === "check"));
    if (blocking.length > 0) return {kind: "off", axes: blocking};
    return {kind: "curve", d: curveRowOf(s), checks: off};
  }
  const statText = d => d.stat_type === "t" ? `t = ${fmtStat(d.stat)} on ${d.df} df` : `z = ${fmtStat(d.stat)}`;
  function checkText(a, code, d) {
    if (a === "inference" && code === "randomisation") return `The randomisation test of this specification, 1,999 reshuffles of the names, gives ${pEq(d.p_ri)}.`;
    if (a === "inference" && code === "chisq") return "The curve stores no chi-square test. Without covariates it tests the same difference as the model, a little more conservatively when R applies its continuity correction.";
    if (a === "scale" && code === "odds_ratio") return d.model === "logit"
      ? `As an odds ratio, the logit coefficient is ${Math.exp(d.coef).toFixed(2)}.`
      : "A linear probability model has no odds ratio; select the logistic regression to read one.";
    if (a === "scale" && code === "r") return `By the rule of the robustness study, the test converts to a partial correlation of ${fmtR(d.r)}.`;
    return "";
  }
  function shortVerdict(v) {
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d;
      const checks = v.checks.map(a => checkText(a, sel[a], d)).join(" ");
      return `On the curve: ${fmtB(d.b_pp)} points (${fmtPct(d.rate_hisp)} against ${fmtPct(d.rate_comp)}), ${statText(d)}, ${pEq(d.p)}; ranked ${d.rank} of 64 from the largest gap.${checks ? " " + checks : ""}`;
    }
    return `Off the curve: ${v.axes.map(a => `${opt(a, sel[a]).decision.toLowerCase()} – ${opt(a, sel[a]).label} (${DM.judgement[opt(a, sel[a]).judgement].toLowerCase()})`).join("; ")}.`;
  }
  function longVerdict(v) {
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d;
      const parts = [`The selection is one of the 64 specifications on the curve. Its estimate is ${fmtB(d.b_pp)} points, ${fmtPct(d.rate_hisp)} of the Hispanic names against ${fmtPct(d.rate_comp)} of the comparison names, on ${d.n} emails, with ${statText(d)} and ${pEq(d.p)}. Ranked from the largest gap, it is number ${d.rank} of the 64.`];
      for (const a of v.checks) parts.push(checkText(a, sel[a], d));
      return parts.join(" ");
    }
    const reasons = v.axes.map(a => {
      const o = opt(a, sel[a]);
      return `${o.decision} – ${o.label}: ${o.reason}`;
    }).join(" ");
    let txt = `The curve holds no analysis with this selection. ${reasons}`;
    if (v.axes.length === 1) {
      const a = v.axes[0];
      const disp = displays.find(d => d.axis === a && d.option === sel[a]);
      if (disp) txt += ` A display beside the curve holds this option at the reference settings (${disp.note}): ${fmtB(disp.b_pp)} points, ${pEq(disp.p)}, on ${disp.n} emails.`;
    } else {
      txt += " Each option off the curve is taught on its own, so this combination was never fitted.";
    }
    return txt + " The burgundy marks are the specifications on the curve that share every other choice.";
  }

  // ---- the map
  const stageEls = {};
  const chipEls = [];
  const verdictBox = el("p", {class: "dm-verdict", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const resetBtn = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-reset"}, "Back to the reference specification");
  const stagesBox = el("div", {class: "dm-stages"});
  DM.stages.forEach((st, si) => {
    const box = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": `dm-stage-${st.id}`},
      el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(si + 1)),
        el("h3", {id: `dm-stage-${st.id}`}, st.title)),
      el("p", {class: "dm-stage-note"}, st.note));
    for (const axis of axesOfStage(st.id)) {
      const opts = optionsOf(axis);
      const first = opts[0];
      const nameId = `dm-dec-${axis}`;
      const group = el("div", {class: "dm-chips", role: "group", "aria-labelledby": nameId});
      for (const o of opts) {
        const tip = o.on_curve ? `${o.label}: on the curve` : `${o.label}: off the curve, ${DM.judgement[o.judgement].toLowerCase()}`;
        const b = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-chip" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${col(axis)}`,
                                "aria-pressed": "false", title: tip, "aria-label": tip, "data-axis": axis, "data-option": o.option}, o.label);
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          const before = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          sel[axis] = o.option;
          latest = axis;
          update(st.id);
          const after = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
        });
        chipEls.push({b, axis, code: o.option});
        group.append(b);
      }
      box.append(el("div", {class: "dm-decision"},
        el("div", {class: "dm-decision-name", id: nameId}, first.decision,
          el("span", {class: "lv", style: `color:${col(axis)}`}, DM.levelShort[first.level])),
        group));
    }
    stageEls[st.id] = box;
    stagesBox.append(box);
  });
  const verdictStage = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": "dm-stage-verdict"},
    el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(DM.stages.length + 1)),
      el("h3", {id: "dm-stage-verdict"}, "The verdict")),
    verdictBox, resetBtn);
  stagesBox.append(verdictStage);
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const before = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
    latest = null;
    update(null);
    const after = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
  });

  // ---- the panel: statement, the selected option, its twins, the curve
  const statementP = el("p", {class: "dm-statement estimand", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const methodP = el("p", {class: "dm-method"});
  const changedNote = el("p", {class: "dm-small"});
  const optionBox = el("div");
  const pairBox = el("div");
  const curveBox = el("div");
  const panel = el("div", {class: "dm-panel", role: "region", "aria-label": "The selection and its results"},
    el("h3", {}, "The estimand statement"), statementP, methodP, changedNote,
    el("h3", {}, "The selected option"), optionBox,
    el("h3", {}, "Against its twins on the curve"), pairBox,
    el("h3", {}, "The curve of 64"), curveBox);
  const side = el("div", {class: "dm-side"});
  const topSlot = el("div");
  const layout = el("div", {class: "dm-layout"}, el("div", {}, topSlot, stagesBox), side);

  const legend = el("div", {class: "dm-legend"},
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0e3b6a"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0f6b6b"}), DM.levelName.estimand),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#4a7a3f"}), DM.levelName.measurement),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#8c5a10"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#7b6a8f"}), DM.levelName.estimation),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample"}, "solid"), "on the curve"),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample off"}, "dashed"), "in the course, off the curve"));

  const wide = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1100px)");
  function place(stageId) {
    if (wide.matches) { if (panel.parentNode !== side) side.append(panel); return; }
    if (stageId === null || stageId === undefined) { if (panel.parentNode !== topSlot) topSlot.append(panel); return; }
    const anchor = stageId === "verdict" ? verdictStage : stageEls[stageId];
    if (anchor.nextSibling !== panel) anchor.after(panel);
  }

  // ---- charts
  function curveChart(width) {
    const onVary = VARY.filter(a => isOn(sel, a));
    const match = curve.filter(d => onVary.every(a => d[a] === sel[a]));
    const matchSet = new Set(match.map(d => d.spec_id));
    const showLatest = latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest);
    const latestRows = showLatest ? curve.filter(d => d[latest] === sel[latest] && !matchSet.has(d.spec_id)) : [];
    const latestSet = new Set(latestRows.map(d => d.spec_id));
    const base = curve.filter(d => !matchSet.has(d.spec_id) && !latestSet.has(d.spec_id));
    const tip = d => `${recipe(d)}\n${fmtB(d.b_pp)} points, ${statText(d)}, ${pEq(d.p)}`;
    const dots = (data, stroke, op, r, sw) => [
      Plot.ruleX(data, {x: "rank", y1: d => d.b_pp - 1.96 * d.se_pp, y2: d => d.b_pp + 1.96 * d.se_pp, stroke, strokeOpacity: op * 0.35, strokeWidth: sw}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p < 0.05), {x: "rank", y: "b_pp", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: tip}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p >= 0.05), {x: "rank", y: "b_pp", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: tip})
    ];
    const ref = curve.filter(d => d.ref === true);
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(230, Math.min(320, Math.round(width * 0.5))), marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 38,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: "The curve of 64 specifications, with the current selection marked",
      x: {domain: [0, 65], label: "64 specifications, ranked from the largest gap →", ticks: 4},
      y: {domain: DM.domainB, label: "↑ Gap in points (Hispanic minus comparison)", grid: true, ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        ...dots(base, "#1d2731", 0.35, 3.4, 0.8),
        ...dots(latestRows, col(latest || "comparison"), 0.75, 3.6, 1),
        ...dots(match, "#8b1538", 1, 5.2, 1.6),
        Plot.text(ref, {x: "rank", y: "b_pp", text: () => "reference", dy: -14, fontSize: 10, fill: "#1d2731"})
      ]
    });
  }
  function pairData(axis, code) {
    const base = baselineOf(axis);
    const others = VARY.filter(a => a !== axis);
    const key = d => others.map(a => d[a]).join("|");
    const baseMap = new Map(curve.filter(d => d[axis] === base).map(d => [key(d), d]));
    const rows = code === base ? curve.filter(d => d[axis] !== base) : curve.filter(d => d[axis] === code);
    return rows.map(d => ({x: baseMap.get(key(d)).b_pp, y: d.b_pp, s: d.p < 0.05, row: d, twin: baseMap.get(key(d))}));
  }
  function pairChart(width, axis, code, data) {
    const c = col(axis);
    const others = VARY.filter(a => a !== axis);
    const isSel = d => others.every(a => d.row[a] === sel[a]) && (code === baselineOf(axis) || d.row[axis] === code);
    const selPair = isOn(sel, axis) ? data.filter(isSel) : [];
    const tip = d => `${recipe(d.row)}\n${fmtB(d.x)} → ${fmtB(d.y)} points`;
    const lo = -22, hi = -10;
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(240, Math.min(340, Math.round(width * 0.6))), marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 40,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: `Each specification on the curve set against its twin with ${opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label}`,
      x: {domain: [lo, hi], label: `with ${opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label.toLowerCase()} (points) →`, ticks: 5},
      y: {domain: [lo, hi], label: "↑ with the other option (points)", ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        Plot.line([[lo, lo], [hi, hi]], {stroke: "#5b6b78", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        Plot.dot(data, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 3.6, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke: c, strokeOpacity: 0.75, strokeWidth: 1, title: tip}),
        Plot.dot(selPair, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 6, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke: "#8b1538", strokeWidth: 1.8, title: tip})
      ]
    });
  }

  // ---- the selected option, in words and numbers
  const curveRange = [d3.min(curve, d => d.b_pp), d3.max(curve, d => d.b_pp)];
  function summaryText(axis, code, o) {
    const out = [];
    if (!o.on_curve) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The course does not cross this option with the curve, so there are no twins to set it against. The verdict below gives the reason and, where a display beside the curve holds the option, its estimate at the reference settings."));
      return out;
    }
    if (!VARY.includes(axis)) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Every specification on the curve uses this option, so there is nothing on the curve to set it against. On the curve the 64 estimates run from ${fmtB(curveRange[0])} to ${fmtB(curveRange[1])} points, and all are significant at 5% under the test of their own model.`));
      return out;
    }
    const base = baselineOf(axis);
    const baseLabel = opt(axis, base).label;
    if (code !== base) {
      const r = devRows.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Against their twins with ${baseLabel.toLowerCase()}, the ${r.n_pairs} specifications with this option move the estimate by ${fmtShift(r.shift_mean)} points on average, from ${fmtShift(r.shift_min)} to ${fmtShift(r.shift_max)}, and ${Math.round(100 * r.sig_share)}% of them stay significant at 5%. A positive shift moves the estimate towards zero.`));
    } else {
      const alts = devRows.filter(d => d.axis === axis && d.option !== base)
        .map(d => `${opt(axis, d.option).label.toLowerCase()} by ${fmtShift(d.shift_mean)} points on average`).join(", ");
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `This is the option against which the others of the decision are compared. Swapped in on twin specifications, the alternatives move the estimate as follows: ${alts}.`));
    }
    return out;
  }

  function renderOption(width) {
    optionBox.replaceChildren();
    pairBox.replaceChildren();
    if (latest === null) {
      optionBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The map opens on the reference specification: Hispanic against white names among the emails that drew a reply, the five replies without a greeting code left out, a difference in proportions without covariates. Select any option on the map to read what it estimates and whether it answers the claim."));
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "Once an option of a decision that varies on the curve is selected, a chart here sets each specification against its twin that differs only in that decision."));
      return;
    }
    const axis = latest, code = sel[axis], o = opt(axis, code), c = col(axis);
    optionBox.append(
      el("p", {class: "dm-option-title"}, `${o.decision}: ${o.label}`),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge", style: `--c:${c}`}, DM.levelName[o.level]),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${o.on_curve ? "#1d2731" : "#8b1538"}`}, DM.judgement[o.judgement]),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, "What it estimates. "), o.estimates),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, o.on_curve ? "Why it is on the curve. " : "Why it is off the curve. "), o.explanation),
      el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Taught on ", pageLink(o.page), "."));
    for (const p of summaryText(axis, code, o)) pairBox.append(p);
    if (o.on_curve && VARY.includes(axis)) {
      const data = pairData(axis, code);
      const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
      box.append(pairChart(width, axis, code, data));
      pairBox.append(box);
      const baseLabel = opt(axis, baselineOf(axis)).label.toLowerCase();
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, code === baselineOf(axis)
        ? `Each mark is one pair: a specification with ${baseLabel}, placed horizontally by its gap, and its twin with another option of the decision, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks above it lie closer to zero. The burgundy marks are the pairs of the current selection.`
        : `Each mark is one pair: a specification with ${baseLabel}, placed horizontally by its gap, and its twin with ${o.label.toLowerCase()}, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks above it lie closer to zero. The burgundy mark is the pair of the current selection.`));
    }
  }

  let lastWidth = 0;
  function drawPanel() {
    const width = Math.max(280, Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34));
    lastWidth = width;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    renderOption(width);
    curveBox.replaceChildren();
    const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
    box.append(curveChart(width));
    curveBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, longVerdict(v)), box,
      el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, `Each mark is one of the 64 specifications on the curve of the claim, ranked from the largest gap, with its 95% confidence interval; below zero, Hispanic names were greeted by name less often. Open circles are significant at 5% under the test of their own model. Burgundy marks are the specifications that match every on-curve choice of the selection${latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest) ? `, and the coloured marks are the other specifications that share the option selected last (${opt(latest, sel[latest]).label})` : ""}. The ink label marks the reference specification.`));
  }

  function update(stageId) {
    for (const {b, axis, code} of chipEls) b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", sel[axis] === code ? "true" : "false");
    const st = statement(sel);
    renderSegments(statementP, st.question);
    renderSegments(methodP, st.method);
    const nowText = {};
    for (const p of [...st.question, ...st.method]) if (typeof p !== "string") nowText[p.key] = p.text;
    const anyChanged = prevText !== null && Object.keys(nowText).some(k => prevText[k] !== nowText[k]);
    changedNote.textContent = (anyChanged ? "The marked phrases are the ones that the latest choice changed. " : "")
      + "Bold phrases state the question, green phrases give the measurement of its outcome, and the second sentence gives the model by which the answer is reached.";
    prevText = nowText;
    verdictBox.textContent = shortVerdict(verdictOf(sel));
    place(stageId);
    drawPanel();
  }

  const root = el("div", {class: "dm"}, legend, layout);
  update(null);
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    const w = Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34);
    if (w > 0 && Math.abs(w - lastWidth) > 24) { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => axesOfStage(s.id).includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); }
  });
  ro.observe(root);
  const onMedia = () => { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => axesOfStage(s.id).includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); };
  wide.addEventListener("change", onMedia);
  invalidation.then(() => { ro.disconnect(); wide.removeEventListener("change", onMedia); });
  return root;
}
```


:::

The three groups of decisions on the map are those of the menu, [set out below](#level-estimand): a decision about the question changes what is asked, a measurement decision changes how the outcome is counted, and a decision about the model changes how the answer is reached. The emails counted are chosen first on the map, among the data, but the choice is a decision about the question, because counting only the replies and counting every delivered email answer two related questions, the tone of the replies that came and the effect of the name on receiving a named greeting at all. The [background page](background.qmd#sec-posttreatment) sets out why the two differ.

## The estimand statement

Write the statement that your analysis will complete:

> Among **which emails**, with **which names**, from **which officials**, the difference in the share that drew **which outcome** between Hispanic names and **which comparison group** (*how uncoded replies and bounced emails are treated*).
>
> Estimated with *which model*, *which adjustment*, tested by *which test* and reported *on which scale*.

The `r xfun::numbers_to_words(n_dec)` decisions fall into three groups, and one question sorts them: would two analysts who chose differently accept each other's number as an answer to the same question? If they would not, the decision belongs to the question, and moving it rewrites a bold slot of the statement. If they would, a decision about how the outcome is counted is a measurement decision and changes only a slot in the brackets, and any other decision belongs to the model and changes only the second sentence. The completed statement is your estimand [@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand], the quantity that your number estimates, and a reader needs it before the number means anything.

## The curve of `r nrow(curve)` {#the-curve}

Five decisions vary on the curve, which gives 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 4 = `r nrow(curve)` specifications, and the other `r xfun::numbers_to_words(length(fixed_axes))` decisions take a single option. The [Specification curve](curve.qmd) page shows all `r nrow(curve)` and the reference specification among them.

Within the curve, what varies is the size of the gap, and @tbl-shifts shows which decisions move it. Each row compares the specifications with an option against their twins that differ only in that decision.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-shifts
#| tbl-cap: "What each option on the curve does to the estimate, against the first option of its decision on twin specifications that agree on every other decision. A positive shift moves the estimate towards zero. Source: `data/menu_deviations.csv`."
#| echo: false
lab <- \(axis, option) menu$label[menu$axis == axis & menu$option == option]
dec <- \(axis) menu$decision[menu$axis == axis][1]
deviations |>
  datawizard::data_filter(option != baseline) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(
    Decision = purrr::map_chr(axis, dec),
    Option = purrr::map2_chr(axis, option, lab),
    Against = purrr::map2_chr(axis, baseline, lab),
    `Mean shift` = sgn(shift_mean, 2),
    Smallest = sgn(shift_min, 2),
    Largest = sgn(shift_max, 2),
    `Still significant` = pct(100 * sig_share, 0)
  ) |>
  datawizard::data_select(c("Decision", "Option", "Against", Pairs = "n_pairs", "Mean shift",
                            "Smallest", "Largest", "Still significant")) |>
  tinytable::tt() |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 4:8, align = "r")
```

Counting all delivered emails moves the estimate by `r sgn(dv("population", "all", "shift_mean"))` points on average, towards zero, and every other option by at most `r fmt(max(abs(deviations$shift_max[deviations$axis != "population"])))` points. Within the original data, the claim holds under every defensible choice, and only its size moves.

## The question {#level-estimand}

Each decision in this group rewrites a bold slot of the statement, so two analysts who decide differently are answering different questions, and their results are not rival estimates of one quantity.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-level1
#| tbl-cap: "The decisions about the question. Options off the curve carry the judgement of the course in brackets. Source: `data/menu_options.csv`."
#| echo: false
judgement_txt <- c(kept = "on the curve", other_question = "another question",
                   weaker_answer = "a weaker answer", check = "a check",
                   unavailable = "not in the public file")
level_table <- \(lv) {
  # dplyr: of the datawizard verbs only data_filter() finds the argument lv,
  # and only from version 1.5.0
  menu |>
    dplyr::filter(level == lv) |>
    dplyr::mutate(item = paste0(label, " <code>", option, "</code>")) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      on = paste(item[on_curve], collapse = "; "),
      off = if (any(!on_curve)) {
        paste0(item[!on_curve], " (", judgement_txt[judgement[!on_curve]], ")", collapse = "; ")
      } else {
        "–"
      },
      .by = c(axis, decision)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Decision = decision, `On the curve` = on, `Off the curve` = off) |>
    tinytable::tt()
}
level_table("estimand")
```

### Outcome

The claim is about tone, and the OAs measure tone by whether a reply opens with the name of the sender, coded leniently so that "Hi Brett" and "Dear Ms. Martinez" both count. The greeting is the outcome of every specification on the curve. The paper also asks whether officials reply at all and whether they reply within 24 hours, which are questions about access rather than tone. On the public file, emails with Hispanic names drew a reply `r fmt(abs(out("reply", "hispanic", "b_pp")))` points less often than emails with white names (`r pe(out("reply", "hispanic", "p"))`, two-sided), and replies to them came within 24 hours `r fmt(out("reply24", "hispanic", "b_pp"))` points more often (`r pe(out("reply24", "hispanic", "p"))`). Both are other claims of the same paper, and both stay off the curve.

### Comparison group

The claim as SCORE selected it compares Hispanic names with white names, and the abstract compares them with "their black and white counterparts". Both readings are defensible, and both are on the curve. Among the coded replies, `r pct(grp("white", "named_pct"))` of replies to white names, `r pct(grp("black", "named_pct"))` of replies to Black names and `r pct(grp("hispanic", "named_pct"))` of replies to Hispanic names opened with the name, so pooling the Black names with the white ones narrows the gap, by `r sgn(dv("comparison", "nonhispanic", "shift_mean"))` points on average across the curve. The comparison of Black with white names, a gap of `r fmt(out("named", "black", "b_pp"))` points among replies (`r pe(out("named", "black", "p"))`), is a separate finding of the paper about another group and stays off the curve.

### Emails counted

This is the decision that moves the estimate most. Counting only the emails that drew a reply is the comparison of the paper, and it answers the question about tone directly, how often the replies that came opened with the name. Counting every delivered email, with a missing reply as no greeting, keeps the groups exactly as randomisation made them, so the difference is an effect of the name on receiving a named greeting, but that outcome mixes whether a reply came with how it began. The first comparison is a pure effect of the name only if the name did not change which officials replied, the post-treatment problem that analyst 25N5D raised and that the [background page](background.qmd#sec-posttreatment) sets out. Both stay on the curve. Counting all emails moves the estimate by `r sgn(dv("population", "all", "shift_mean"))` points on average (from `r sgn(dv("population", "all", "shift_min"))` to `r sgn(dv("population", "all", "shift_max"))`), mostly because fewer than six in ten emails drew any reply: at the reference settings the shares become `r pct(all_twin$rate_hisp)` against `r pct(all_twin$rate_comp)`.

### Names

The paper pools the male and the female name of each group, and the claim speaks of Hispanic applicants in general, so the curve pools them too. The two halves differ. Among replies, the gap between Santiago and Brett is `r fmt(sub_("male", "b_pp"))` points (`r pe(sub_("male", "p"))`, n = `r sub_("male", "n")`) and the gap between Gabriela and Emily `r fmt(sub_("female", "b_pp"))` points (`r pe(sub_("female", "p"))`, n = `r sub_("female", "n")`). Either half answers a narrower question, about men or about women, and the SCORE replication used male names only.

### Who replied

The OAs coded whether the official who replied had a distinctively Hispanic name, to test whether Hispanic officials treat Hispanic applicants better. That is a separate hypothesis, and the subgroup is selected after the email arrived, which is the post-treatment problem again. It is also small: among the `r sub_("replies from officials", "n")` replies to Hispanic and white names that came from officials with Hispanic names, the gap is `r fmt(sub_("replies from officials", "b_pp"))` points (`r pe(sub_("replies from officials", "p"))`), against `r fmt(sub_("replies from other", "b_pp"))` points among the `r sub_("replies from other", "n")` replies from other officials. The curve keeps every reply.

## Measurement {#level-measurement}

The question stays the same, and these decisions change how the outcome is counted.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-level2
#| tbl-cap: "The measurement decisions. Source: `data/menu_options.csv`."
#| echo: false
level_table("measurement")
```

### Replies without a greeting code

The file holds `r sum(housing$reply %in% 1 & is.na(housing$named))` replies without a greeting code. Leaving them out is what a model does by default and what four of the five analysts did. Counting them as replies without a greeting is a defensible reading, since a reply in which the coders found no greeting probably did not open with a name, and analyst 25N5D made that choice without stating it, by keeping the three of them that went to white and Hispanic names in the counts of emails. Both stay on the curve, and the choice moves the estimate by `r sgn(dv("uncoded", "not_named", "shift_mean"), 2)` points on average.

### Bounced emails

Of the emails sent, `r sum(is.na(housing$reply))` bounced, `r bounced_by("white")` with white names, `r bounced_by("black")` with Black names and `r bounced_by("hispanic")` with Hispanic names, and they carry no reply status. They never reached an official, so none of them holds the response of an official to a name, but the bounces are uneven across the six sending accounts, one for each name, as the [missing-values module](companion/missingness.qmd#sec-bounced) shows. Every specification on the curve leaves the bounced emails out. Counting them as unanswered adds rows whose outcome was settled by a broken address. It matters only when all emails are counted, since a bounced email is never a reply: there it moves the gap from `r fmt(bounced_twin$b_pp)` to `r fmt(bounced_b)` points, a small change, but one that was produced by broken addresses rather than by officials.

## The model {#level-estimation}

With the question and the outcome fixed, these decisions change the model that is fitted, the test and the scale on which the answer is reported.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-level3
#| tbl-cap: "The decisions about the model. Source: `data/menu_options.csv`."
#| echo: false
level_table("estimation")
```

### Model form {#model}

A linear probability model, a linear regression of the 0/1 outcome, gives the difference in proportions as its coefficient, and without covariates it is exactly the difference between the two observed shares. Its standard errors are taken with the HC2 correction, which allows the variance of a 0/1 outcome to differ between the groups. A logistic regression models the log odds of a greeting, and the course reports it as an average marginal effect, the difference in the predicted probability of a greeting between Hispanic and white names, averaged over the analysed emails. Without covariates the two give the same estimate, and with covariates they differ by at most `r fmt(max(abs(c(dv("model", "logit", "shift_min"), dv("model", "logit", "shift_max")))), 2)` points across the curve.

The OAs, EWFMI and P9W8Y fitted all three groups of names in one model and read off the Hispanic–white contrast. Without covariates this gives exactly the two-group difference, as the refit of P9W8Y shows (`r fmt(mark("P9W8Y", "b_pp"))` points). With the covariates of the paper in thirds, the three-group logit gives `r fmt(mark("OA_blinded", "b_pp"))` points against `r fmt(three_twin$b_pp)` for the two-group logit, because the emails with Black names then help to estimate the covariates. The three-group model is a check rather than a separate answer.

### Adjustment

Because the names were assigned at random, the groups of authorities differ only by chance, and the raw difference answers the claim without covariates. Covariates in an experiment buy precision rather than freedom from bias, so every adjustment that uses information recorded before the emails went out is defensible, and all four sets stay on the curve: none; the hard-to-find address; that with the thirds of population and poverty, the set left by the instruction of the robustness study of SCORE [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]; and that with the thirds of percent Black and percent Hispanic as well, the covariates of Table 1 in the form that the public file allows. The adjustments move the estimate by `r sgn(dv("adjust", "email", "shift_mean"), 2)`, `r sgn(dv("adjust", "place", "shift_mean"), 2)` and `r sgn(dv("adjust", "place_ethnic", "shift_mean"), 2)` points on average. Part of the shift under the two community sets comes from the emails that they lose, since `r no_thirds` authorities have no community thirds.

The sex of the name is balanced by design, one male and one female name in each group, and adjusting for it changes almost nothing: at the reference settings the gap becomes `r fmt(sex_b)` points (`r pe(sex_p)`). It is a check. The continuous census values of the paper cannot be used at all, because the public file replaces them with thirds to protect the authorities, which is why no one outside the original team can fit the published model exactly.

### Test

Each specification is tested by its own model, HC2 errors for the linear model and the usual z test for the logit, which is what a single analyst would report. Three other tests are checks. The randomisation test needs no model of the errors, only the fact that the names were assigned at random, and it agrees with the model tests on every specification. The $\chi^2$ test of a two-by-two table tests the same difference without a model, and `chisq.test()` in R applies the continuity correction to such a table unless it is told otherwise: on the comparison of 8PTRZ it gives $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(chi_yates$statistic, 3)` with the correction and `r fmt(chi_plain$statistic, 2)` without it. A one-tailed test halves the p-value by deciding the direction in advance, and the paper uses one for the gap in replies, whose two-sided p of `r fmt(out("reply", "hispanic", "p"), 3)` becomes the `r fmt(out("reply", "hispanic", "p") / 2, 2)` of the paper. It is defensible only when the direction was fixed before anyone looked at the data, so the curve keeps two-sided tests.

### Effect scale

The claim, in the abstract, states the gap in percentage points, which a reader can picture without a formula, and every point of the curve is placed on that scale. The odds ratio is the scale of the logistic regression itself, and across the `r nrow(logit_or)` logit specifications it runs from `r fmt(min(logit_or$or), 2)` to `r fmt(max(logit_or$or), 2)`. Odds ratios change when covariates are added even in a randomised experiment, because they compare odds within groups of similar emails rather than averaging over all of them, so the course reports the logit in points instead. The partial correlation is the scale of the robustness study, which runs from `r fmt(min(curve$r), 3)` to `r fmt(max(curve$r), 3)` on the curve, and which depends on the number of emails and the shares in each group as well as on the gap, as the [background page](background.qmd#sec-scale) shows.

## Worked example

**Choice:** comparison `white`, emails counted `all`, replies without a code `not_named`, model `lpm`, adjustment `none`; male and female names, any official, bounced emails left out, the test of the model, percentage points.

**Justification, by group of decisions.** The claim as selected compares Hispanic with white names, so the white names are the comparison. Counting every delivered email keeps the groups as randomisation made them, so the difference is an effect of the name and does not depend on which officials chose to reply, at the cost of an outcome that combines replying with greeting. A reply without a greeting code most probably did not open with a name. The names were randomised, so the raw difference in proportions needs no covariates, and its HC2 test is the test that a single analyst would report.

The specification gives `r fmt(bounced_twin$b_pp)` points (`r pct(bounced_twin$rate_hisp)` against `r pct(bounced_twin$rate_comp)`), t = `r fmt(bounced_twin$stat, 2)` on `r bounced_twin$df` df. A justification of this kind connects each choice to the wording of the claim or to the design, according to the group to which the choice belongs, and it is what the preregistration of Task 5 asks you to write before you run the model.
